recorded-direction.text: The project treats terminals as lightweight Web2 applications with cryptographic capabilities. Purpose and risk guide verification before transaction construction or off-chain data consumption. The diagram distinguishes design inputs, executable model, reviewed contract and implementation. Own-anchor independence, chosen institutional publications and separately purchased availability remain the trust and economic direction.

named-deployment-roles.text: Anchors and ledgers run nodes. Anchors serve signed roots; ledgers serve data and proofs. Applications serve application proofs. Terminals consume all three, verify them and build transactions or drive real-world effects. The names describe roles rather than a fixed deployment count.

words-that-constrain-the-design.text: The rulings require immutable content separate from chainpoint indexes, independent per-block anchor publication and an API governed by coherent evidence rather than Koios compatibility. Historical CBOR can be untrusted reconstruction material. The preserved present-validity and future-validation ruling distinguishes off-chain ledger membership checks from application proofs used in redeemers.

claims-and-evidence-boundaries.text: The root, session and ledger model makes a bounded executable contribution. Root acceptance establishes terminal endorsement, acquisition preserves the exact selected point and ledger verification binds the same witnessed object to the independent root and its asset and datum observations. Honest unique output and application root soundness requires separate correspondence, witness, encoding, interpretation and OneShot premises. Membership alone does not imply uniqueness, completeness, canonicality or settlement. This is model evidence rather than a full system verifier or deployment. Trust and operating choices are not measured price rankings.

what-remains-unproved.text: Concrete anchor policy selection, key rotation, signed encodings, freshness and rollback notices remain open. The ledger model binds the witnessed asset and datum under explicit hypotheses; application replay, nested proof and transition bindings need their own evidence. Archive coverage, provider interoperability, cost commitments and settlement remain unresolved.

evidence-available-today.text: Pinned Lean proofs and scenarios establish root acceptance, exact point session behavior and ledger answer verification. The ledger soundness statement identifies an honest member, actual asset, honest datum root and unique asset bearing pair under separate selected point correspondence, witness, encoding, interpretation and OneShot hypotheses. Honest fixtures inhabit all premises with acceptance. Real production provider root substitutions accept an impostor and constructively refute the unchanged guarantee. Two honest same asset outputs with different datum roots refute the full unique output guarantee after only OneShot is removed. All three ledger scenarios exercise the verifier. Inherited repeated reads, expiry refusal, release and no substitution controls remain. Branch and lease policy, independent acceptance, remote CI, component implementation and deployment require separate evidence. Existing MPFS verification and inspected Koios and Blockfrost interfaces remain prior bounded evidence.
